blocks.x: Álvaro Arbeloa played in some great defences but whether he knows how to coach one remains to be seen. ­Fulham have been fragile since appointing the Spaniard and they were fortunate not to be dragged into a penalty shootout by West Ham as this entertainingCarabao Cup tie drew to a close.

West Ham equalised twice during the first half and they almost did it again after Oscar Bobb made it 3-2 in the 78th minute. Nuno Espírito Santo raged at a poor miss from Taty ­Castellanos, though, and Fulham clambered into the last 16 after resisting late pressure from the ­Championship pacesetters.

It was a mixed bag as far as ­Fulham were concerned. West Ham were beaten but not outplayed and will not mind switching focus back to their promotion push. They stretched Fulham. Arbeloa played an experimental lineup and the performance was not convincing. César Palacios finished with a goal and an assist but Kevin and Emile Smith Rowe disappointed and the Premier League side needed Bobb and Josh King to make the difference after coming off the bench.

“I was a bit upset at half-time,” Arbeloa said. “I am asking how we can concede these two goals. So easy for me. We need to improve there. We need to be more aggressive when defending. In the end we need a massive save. If we are not aggressive enough it is my job to improve my players. We have to work a lot.”

Before kick-off there was a moving tribute to Ludek Miklosko, the legendary former West Ham goalkeeper, after he passed away this week at the age of 64. It added emotion to the tie, ensuring the hosts were not short of motivation against the hardest side they have faced since last season’s relegation.

Although West Ham rested key players in attack before visiting ­Millwall on Saturday they responded well after going behind in the 13th minute. They tested Fulham in the air and levelled when Arne Engels’ deep cross found Konstantinos Mavropanos, who rose at the far post and headed across for his fellow defender Morato to nod in his first goal since joining from Nottingham Forest on loan this month.

blocks.x: Peterborough moved into the fourth round of the Carabao Cup for the first time since 2009 thanks to a 7-6 penalty shootout victory over Barnsley that followed a thrilling 3-3 draw between the two League One sides.

Barnsley were handed the lead after 61 seconds when a clearance by the Peterborough goalkeeper, Alex Bass, was charged down by Cameron McGeehan, with the Tykes captain nodding in after the ball had come off the bar.
Peterborough equalised in the 19th minute when Lucca Mendonca’s cross was pushed out by the Barnsley goalkeeper, Kieran Flavell, as far as Harry Leonard, who prodded in.

The hosts then completed the turnaround after 27 minutes when Harley Mills’ free-kick was headed in by the unmarked Danny Ormerod. But the Tykes were level five minutes before half-time when Reyes Cleary beat Mendonca with ease down the left before placing his shot into the bottom corner.
The visitors looked to have won it when Cleary bent in his second in the 74th minute, but Ormerod sent the tie to penalties with by heading in Mills’ cross with just two minutes remaining.
After 12 successful spot-kicks, a tame effort from Barnsley’s Luke Alker was saved by Bass, giving Harrison Jones the chance to send the hosts through, which he dispatched.

Brentford emerged from a tense finish against Reading to book their place in the Carabao Cup fourth round with a 2-1 victory. Callum Wilson and Fabio Carvalho were on target in the first half as the Premier League club showed a clinical touch against League One opposition, who produced a number of chances but lacked the firepower to finish them off. Paudie O’Connor eventually pulled one back to revive Reading’s challenge and Brentford could not rest easy in the remaining 18 minutes, although the substitute Igor Thiago was among those who should have killed the match off.
